extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners (agents/attorneys), and USPTO personnel
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and substantive requirements for preparing, filing, correcting, and treating Application Data Sheets (ADS) in U.S. patent applications (including use of PLT/PCT forms and pre-/post-AIA distinctions). Covers required bibliographic elements, signatures, timing, inconsistency resolution, and correction formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADS must be titled and contain required section headings
rubrics_metrics.description: An application data sheet must be titled "Application Data Sheet" and must contain all of the section headings listed in paragraph (b) of 37 CFR 1.76, with any appropriate data for each section heading. If an application data sheet is provided, the application data sheet is part of the provisional or nonprovisional application for which it has been submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If provided, the ADS is part of the application; it must include every section heading in 1.76(b) (bibliographic elements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant information content
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant information includes the name, residence, mailing address, and citizenship of each applicant (§ 1.41(b)). The name of each applicant must include the family name and at least one given name without abbreviation together with any other given name or initial. If the applicant is not an inventor, this information also includes the applicant’s authority (§§ 1.42, 1.43, and 1.47) to apply for the patent on behalf of the inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leave the applicant heading blank if the applicant is the inventor or the remaining joint inventor(s) (37 CFR 1.45). If application is filed by assignee/person with proprietary interest (37 CFR 1.46), the ADS must specify that assignee/person in the applicant information section; name changes and corrections must comply with 37 CFR 1.46(c) and related rules (3.71, 3.73).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee information does not substitute for recorded assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing assignee information in the application data sheet does not substitute for compliance with any requirement of 37 CFR part 3 to have an assignment recorded by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including assignee info in the ADS is considered a request to include such information on the patent application publication; assignment information must be recorded to have legal effect. Assignees who are applicants will appear as applicant; provide assignee information in assignee section only if identification as assignee on publication is desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence information requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence information includes the correspondence address, which may be indicated by reference to a customer number, to which correspondence is to be directed (see § 1.33(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes to correspondence address must comply with 37 CFR 1.33(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application information elements to include
rubrics_metrics.description: Application information includes the title of the invention, a suggested classification by class and subclass, the Technology Center (TC) to which the subject matter is assigned, the total number of drawing sheets, a suggested drawing figure for publication (in a nonprovisional application), any docket number, the type of application, and whether the application discloses subject matter under a secrecy order; for plant apps, include Latin genus/species and variety denomination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested classification and TC should be supplied for provisional apps too (based on disclosure). The Office no longer relies on suggested classification/TC for assignment, and it is not bound to use the suggested drawing figure for publication front page (but will use it if included on a compliant ADS timely filed before publication processing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative (practitioner) information
rubrics_metrics.description: Representative information includes the registration number of each practitioner having a power of attorney in the application (preferably by reference to a customer number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing this information in the ADS does not itself constitute a power of attorney in the application (see § 1.32).

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic priority (benefit) information in ADS constitutes required specific reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Domestic priority information includes the application number, filing date, status (including patent number if available), and relationship of each application for which a benefit is claimed under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), 120, 121, or 365(c). Providing this information in the ADS constitutes the specific reference required by 35 U.S.C. 119(e) or 120 and need not be made part of the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If continuity data are included only in an ADS and not in the specification, the patent front page will take continuity data from the ADS. Pre-AIA 1.76(b)(5) does not apply to provisional applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign priority information in ADS constitutes priority claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign priority information includes the application number, country, and filing date of each foreign application for which priority is claimed. Providing this information in the ADS constitutes the claim for priority as required by 35 U.S.C. 119(b) and § 1.55(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-AIA 1.76(b)(6) does not apply to provisional applications. The patent statute does not require any particular form for a foreign priority claim, but if a corrected ADS is used to add a priority claim it must show the entire claim with underlining relative to the most recent filing receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental/Corrected ADS format and markup rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplemental (corrected) ADS must identify the information that is being changed, preferably with underlining for insertions and strike-through or brackets for text removed. A corrected ADS filed after the filing date of the application or after submission of a first ADS is considered a corrected (or updated) ADS even if an ADS was not previously submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification of changes is not required for an ADS included with an initial submission under 35 U.S.C. 371. A corrected ADS may include all section headings or only those sections containing changed information. For example, additions of benefit/priority claims must be underlined (the entire claim underlined); deletions must be strike-through or bracketed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and entry of corrected ADS (limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: A corrected ADS may be submitted until payment of the issue fee to correct or update information in a previously submitted ADS or in an inventor’s oath/declaration or otherwise of record. However, a corrected ADS filed after final rejection or allowance is not entered as a matter of right and must comply with 37 CFR 1.116 or 1.312, respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should file a corrected ADS with a request for a corrected filing receipt unless accompanied by other actions (e.g., request under 1.48 or 1.46(c) or submission of power of attorney). Certain changes (inventorship, foreign priority, domestic benefit, correspondence address) must comply with their respective rules (1.48, 1.55, 1.78, 1.33(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrected Web-based ADS recommended and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of the corrected Web-based ADS is recommended because it will pre-populate with information from the most recent filing receipt and create a PDF with appropriate strike-through and underlining.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A corrected Web-based ADS is not permitted in national stage applications under 35 U.S.C. 371, provisional applications, plant applications, reexamination proceedings, and supplemental examinations under 35 U.S.C. 257. See USPTO Quick Start Guide for Corrected Web-based ADS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inconsistencies — latest submission generally governs
rubrics_metrics.description: For inconsistencies between information supplied by an ADS and other documents, the latest submitted information will govern notwithstanding whether supplied by an ADS, an amendment to the specification, a designation of a correspondence address, or by an oath/declaration, except as otherwise provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inconsistencies — ADS governs when supplied concurrently
rubrics_metrics.description: The information in the application data sheet will govern when the inconsistent information is supplied at the same time by an amendment to the specification, a designation of correspondence address, or an oath/declaration. The ADS will also govern when inconsistent with information supplied at any time in PLT/PCT model forms or PCT Request Forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is 37 CFR 1.76(d)(2). If another document submitted concurrently contains more accurate information, a corrected ADS should be submitted to conform the ADS to the correct information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath/declaration governs inventorship and citizenship
rubrics_metrics.description: The oath or declaration under § 1.63 or § 1.67 governs inconsistencies with the application data sheet in the naming of inventors (§ 1.41(a)(1)) and setting forth their citizenship (35 U.S.C. 115).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When inventorship or citizenship conflicts arise between ADS and oath/declaration, the oath/declaration controls (37 CFR 1.76(d)(3)). Changes to inventorship must be pursued under 37 CFR 1.48.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office captures bibliographic information from ADS
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will capture bibliographic information from the application data sheet. The Office will generally not review the inventor’s oath/declaration to determine if the bibliographic information contained therein is consistent with the bibliographic information captured from an ADS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captured bibliographic information derived from an ADS containing errors may be corrected by applicant submitting a request and a supplemental ADS under 37 CFR 1.76(c). Examples illustrate that the filing receipt will reflect ADS-captured data even if oath has correct data; correction requires submitting corrected ADS or appropriate rule-based requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirement — unsigned ADS treated as transmittal letter
rubrics_metrics.description: An application data sheet must be signed in compliance with 37 CFR 1.33(b). An unsigned ADS will be treated only as a transmittal letter and will not be effective to provide the name of the inventor for any invention claimed in the application, name as the applicant an assignee/obligated assignee/person with proprietary interest, make a claim to priority of a foreign application, or make a claim to the benefit of a prior-filed domestic application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure ADS is properly signed to effectuate inventor/applicant/priority/benefit information; otherwise those items will have no legal effect via the unsigned ADS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of PLT Model International Forms and PCT Request Form can satisfy ADS requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement in 37 CFR 1.55 or 1.78 for presentation of a priority or benefit claim in an ADS will be satisfied by presentation of such claim in the Patent Law Treaty Model International Request Form; similarly, the requirement in 37 CFR 1.57(a) for reference to previously filed application, and the requirement in 37 CFR 1.46 for presentation of the name of the applicant under 35 U.S.C. 118, will be satisfied by presentation in the appropriate PLT forms or the PCT Request Form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For national stage applications under 35 U.S.C. 371, presentation of a benefit claim in the PCT Request Form or presence of the claim on the front page of the PCT publication under PCT Art. 21(2) will satisfy ADS requirements (37 CFR 1.76(f),(g)). However, ADS information will govern if inconsistent per 1.76(d)(2). Submission of PCT Request Form in an application under 35 U.S.C. 111 must be accompanied by a clear indication that treatment as an application under 35 U.S.C. 111 is desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural requirements when adding/deleting benefit or priority claims
rubrics_metrics.description: When adding a domestic benefit or foreign priority claim in a corrected ADS relative to the most recent filing receipt, the entire benefit or priority claim must be underlined. If an ADS identified an incorrect benefit claim, the corrected ADS should show the deletion with strike-through or brackets and the addition with underlining. Deleting a domestic benefit or foreign priority claim requires a corrected ADS identifying the deletion with strike-through or brackets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If adding or correcting claims outside the statutory time period, a petition for unintentionally delayed claim under 37 CFR 1.78(c) or 1.55(e) may be required. Applicants are cautioned that deleting a benefit or priority claim may expose the application to new prior art or be considered intentionally waiving the claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional ADS sections: publication and access authorizations
rubrics_metrics.description: The ADS form provides sections where applicants can make a request not to publish the application or a request for early publication, and a section to provide an Authorization to Permit Access to the Instant Application by Participating Offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Authorization box is checked, the Office has authority to provide access to the instant patent application to participating foreign offices in which a foreign application claiming priority is filed.
